title: Toast wraps at half the viewport width on phones: tall broken pill over content
devices: iPhone (all phones); also iPad/Mac for long toasts (wraps at 410/735px)
evidence: shots/shell/toast-iphone.png; eval rect [100.5,735.5,201,78.5]; css/components.css:389-405 (#toast: position fixed; inset-inline-start:50%; translate(-50%) with shrink-to-fit width)
rootCause: A fixed element with left:50% gets an available width of (viewport - 50%) for shrink-to-fit sizing, so text wraps at 50% of the viewport before the max-inline-size ever applies.
fix: Give the toast an explicit fit-content width independent of its left offset: e.g. inset-inline:0; margin-inline:auto; inline-size:fit-content; max-inline-size:min(var(--toast-max), calc(100% - var(--sp-32))); transform only on Y. Use a rounded-rect radius (r-16) when it wraps, or keep pill only for one line.
detail: Any toast longer than ~25 characters on iPhone wraps into a 201px-wide, 3-line 'pill' (radius pill on a tall box) sitting over the page content above the tab bar. Reproduced with KOS.ui.toast('You already had 44 badge tiers — they are on the Badge Wall.') at 402x874: rect x=100.5 w=201 h=78.5. Same on every width: the toast can never be wider than half the viewport.

title: Global Backspace = Back fires even when a page handled the key: Backspace on a Money row opens 'Delete this entry?' AND navigates to the previous page underneath
evidence: shots/shell/backspace-money-dialog-over-home.png; eval result {hash:'#/home', dialog:'Delete this entry? QA coffee, −£4.50…'}; js/main.js:20-28; js/modules/money.js:610
rootCause: The shell's history shortcut ignores defaultPrevented and treats any non-text target as free to navigate.
fix: In main.js return early when e.defaultPrevented, when a dialog is open, or when the target is inside [role=listbox]/[data-keys]; better, drop bare Backspace and keep Alt+←/→ (and ⌘[ / ⌘] on the Mac). Register the listener in the bubble phase after page handlers (it already is) and respect defaultPrevented.
detail: js/main.js binds Backspace (outside text fields) to KOS.back() on document and never checks e.defaultPrevented. Money's transaction list uses Delete/Backspace on a focused row to delete it (money.js:610) and calls preventDefault, but the document listener still runs: reproduced on #/money/transactions → focus a row → Backspace: the confirm dialog opens while the route has already changed to #/home behind it; cancelling leaves the user on Home, having lost their place. Any future in-page Backspace handler (ink lasso selection, lists, the editor's rows, Mind's list at mindui.js:154 which is inside a textarea so is safe) collides the same way. Backspace-as-Back is also surprising on its own: a stray Backspace with focus on any button (after clicking a card, closing a menu) leaves the page; browsers removed this shortcut for that reason.

title: Enter on a focused Cancel button CONFIRMS a non-danger confirm dialog (End session, Turn off notifications, Disconnect GitHub, Add a copy/Open existing...)
evidence: eval: {enterOnCancel:'YES'}; js/core/ui.js:291-292 (function onKey(e){ if (e.key==='Enter' && !opts.danger) close(true); } on document); 51 ui.confirm call sites, the non-danger ones listed by grep in js/modules/focus.js, notifications.js, code.js, cardstats.js, governor-ui.js:450, jarun.js, medview.js, pwa.js:53
rootCause: The affirmative Enter shortcut is bound at document level and ignores which control has focus.
fix: Only treat Enter as yes when the target is not a button/link (e.g. if (e.key==='Enter' && !opts.danger && !(e.target.closest && e.target.closest('button,a,[role=button]'))) close(true)); or drop the document listener and rely on the focused confirm button's native Enter.
detail: KOS.ui.confirm adds a document keydown listener that calls close(true) on any Enter when !opts.danger, without looking at the event target. Keydown fires before the focused button's click, so Tab to Cancel (or 'Stay', 'Add a copy') and pressing Enter runs the affirmative action. Reproduced: confirm({title:'Replace?'}) -> focus Cancel -> Enter -> onYes ran. Affected non-danger confirms include Focus 'End early?' (ends and pays the session), 'Turn off closed-app notifications?', 'Disconnect the GitHub App?', 'Reset every permission?', 'Free up space', 'Keep in my cloud', 'Back to the defaults?' (FSRS), the sample/empty account switch, Japanese 'Leave the session?', the vault 'Already in the vault' (Enter on 'Add a copy' opens the existing entry instead) and the service-worker 'Update ready'. Keyboard and switch users on the Mac and iPad keyboard are affected.

title: 'Skip to content' navigates to Home instead of skipping: href='#main' is read by the hash router as an unknown route
evidence: eval mac: {before:'#/calendar', after:'#/home', active:'main'}; index.html:61; js/core/router.js:302-306 (hashchange -> onPop -> parse fails -> home())
rootCause: An in-page fragment link in an app that uses the fragment for routing.
fix: Give the link a click handler that preventDefault()s and calls document.getElementById('main').focus({preventScroll:false}) (or make router.parse ignore hashes that do not start with '#/').

Activating it changes location.hash to '#main'; router.js's hashchange listener parses it, finds no such route and calls home(), so from #/calendar the keyboard user lands on #/home with a new history entry replaced. The one bypass mechanism for keyboard and switch users (WCAG 2.4.1) throws them off the page they were on.

title: KOS.rerender() throws the page back to the top on every device: it saves/restores #main.scrollTop but #stage is the scroller
evidence: eval: {'#/home': ['stage', 600, 0]}; eval reminders {b:[900,0], afterRerender:0, after Back: 0}; scroller probe: #stage overflow-y auto (scrollHeight 2152 / client 772), #main overflow visible; js/core/ui.js:353-356 (var top = main.scrollTop … main.scrollTop = top), js/core/ui.js:1521-1523 (main.innerHTML = ''; main.scrollTop = 0); iPhone eval ['stage',800,0]
rootCause: The scroll container moved from #main to #stage (layout) but ui.js still saves/restores #main.scrollTop, which is always 0.
fix: Introduce one KOS.ui.scrollRoot() (the #stage on wide layouts, document.scrollingElement on the phone) and use it in rerender (save before, restore after the view drew, and again on the next frame for async content) and in show() (reset to 0 on a real navigation; restore a remembered position per history index on Back/Forward, like the router already keeps args per index). Add a smoke test.

Browser Back to a long page also lands at the top (reminders 900 → Home → Back → 0). This contradicts the router contract ('a background pull that repaints the page you are on leaves … your scroll position exactly as they were', router.js:25-29, invariant 65) and the standing 'lost position on redraw' rule. title: Navigating to the page you are already on pushes a duplicate history entry, so Back appears to do nothing
evidence: eval: {d0:2,d1:3,d2:5,h1:'#/calendar'} and {d0:7,d1:9,hash:'#/home'}; js/core/router.js:226-238 (pushEntry when !opts._nav, no route===lastRendered check)

detail: KOS.show() always calls pushEntry() unless it is a _nav redraw; it never compares the new route with lastRendered. Clicking the rail item of the current section, the brand mark on Home, a subject pill for the open subject or a search result for the page in view each add an identical entry. title: Toast 'Undo' is unreachable without a pointer: the button is tabindex=-1 inside the aria-hidden #toast, and the spoken message never says Undo exists

title: Search ranks specification hits in syllabus order, not by relevance: 'binary' shows 'Fields, records and files' first and cuts 'Unsigned binary', 'Two's complement' and Code's 'Binary search trees' past the six shown
evidence: eval: search('binary') title hits at indexes [1,3,4,7,8,12,14,15] of 30; listbox options for 'binary','integration','dijkstra' (printed); js/core/search.js:31 (PER_DOMAIN 6), :42-49 (rank), :60-73 (specDomain: res.slice(0, PER_DOMAIN), no rank); js/modules/hub.js searchSpec (returns specHits in index order)
rootCause: Spec search is a filter, not a ranker, and the cross-domain layer truncates before ranking.
fix: Score spec hits: exact title > title word-start > title contains > spec text > flashcard, then subject order; rank before slicing; add a final 'See all N results' option that opens a results page (or expands the domain).
detail: The Specification domain takes KOS.hub.search's first six results without ranking: the hits come in SEARCH_INDEX order (CS 4.1… then Maths then Code), and search.js's rank() (title-starts-with first) is applied to every other domain but not to spec. For 'binary' 30 leaves match; title matches sit at positions 1,3,4,7,8,12,14,15 so 'Unsigned binary and binary arithmetic' (7), 'Signed binary using two's complement' (8) and all of Code's never appear, while 'Fields, records and files' (body text 'binary file') is first. 'integration' lists 'Partial fractions' above 'Integration as limit of a sum'; 'dijkstra' lists 'Kinds of abstraction' and 'Reverse Polish notation' (flashcard matches). There is no 'show all results' row, so a result past six cannot be reached.

title: One toast slot: each new toast replaces the last, so in the Daily Review (or Home's Today ticks) only the most recent triage can be undone; toasts also vanish after a fixed 2.6 s whatever their length
evidence: js/core/ui.js:71-87 (single node, textContent replace, fixed 2600/8000 ms); Undo toasts at js/modules/dayreview.js:534, :615, :621, :622; js/modules/hub.js:964; js/modules/reminders.js:344
rootCause: The toast is a single-slot primitive and Undo was layered on it without a queue.

The Daily Review's triage buttons (Tomorrow, ✓ Done, Study block, the step actions) each show "<title> · marked done — Undo"; triaging three items in a row leaves only the third's Undo — the first two are committed with no way back, although invariant 144 promises Undo for every change a review makes. Plain toasts last 2.6 s regardless of length: "You already had 44 badge tiers — they are on the Wall." or an error with its reason cannot be read in that time (and the toast cannot be paused by hover or focus).

title: Hold-⌘ shortcut sheet is a fixed list: it shows Ink/PDF/Flashcard keys on every page and omits the shortcuts that exist (Backspace back, Esc, Money row keys, the Daily Review and routine player arrows and S, the story keys, the quiz arrow)

title: KOS.show with an unknown view id draws a blank page and pushes it into history (#/archive, #/nonsense) instead of falling back like a typed URL does
evidence: shots/shell/archive-empty-mac.png (blank main at #/archive); eval {has:false, h3:"#/nonsense", mainLen:0}; js/core/ui.js:1592; js/core/router.js:226-238
rootCause: Unknown-route handling exists only in the hashchange/popstate path, not in KOS.show.
fix: In KOS.show, if !KOS.views[viewId] log a console.warn and redirect to home with replace (same rule as router invalid routes) before pushing any entry.

title: Every cloud pull/merge redraws the active view unconditionally — even when nothing the view shows changed, and even while the user is mid-task
devices: iPad primarily (app switching + Pencil study), all
evidence: js/core/cloudsync.js:487-497 (mergeRemoteIn -> rerenderCurrent), :723-733 (rerenderCurrent -> KOS.rerender), :773-777, :533-560 (conflict path), :1447-1459 (noteChange push), :1480-1495 (Realtime), :1541-1553 (interval/visible/focus); js/core/ui.js:344-357 (rerender: only inkUI.busy guard). Harness: KOS.rerender() reproduces every reset in the other findings.
rootCause: full remount used as the generic refresh for background state changes, with no busy/changed gating
fix: Systemic redraw policy: (1) cloudsync passes what changed (top-level keys that differ between pre- and post-merge state, cheap JSON compare per key) to KOS.rerender({changed:[...], background:true}); views declare the state keys they read (KOS.views.x.reads = ['srs','edits',...]) and are skipped when untouched. (2) A background redraw is DEFERRED while the page is 'busy': a dialog or menu open, focus in an input/textarea/contenteditable, a study engine mounted and touched in the last N minutes (flashcards/quiz/exam/japanese session/code task), pointer down, or within 30 s of the last interaction — instead show a quiet 'Updated on another device · Refresh' chip, and redraw on the next navigation. (3) For views that must refresh live, give them a refresh(changed) hook that patches in place instead of a full remount.
detail: cloudsync.rerenderCurrent() calls KOS.rerender() after every applied remote state: the clean path (applyRemoteState, cloudsync.js:775), the merge path (mergeRemoteIn, :495, also used by a push that lost its compare-and-set race, :533-560) and first link (:1279). There is no check of whether the merged document differs in anything the current view reads, no check that the user is interacting, a dialog/menu is open, an input has focus, or a study engine is running. The only guard in KOS.rerender is the ink pen (ui.js:347). Triggers that reach it: another device's push -> Realtime 'changed' (1.5 s debounce, :1483); returning to the app (visibilitychange/focus, :1548-1552, at most once a minute) — on the iPad every app switch; the 15-min interval; and the iPad's OWN ratings: each store.save -> noteChange -> push after 4 s -> if the Mac/iPhone pushed meanwhile the CAS fails -> conflict() -> mergeRemoteIn -> rerender. An idle open Mac pushes on its own (achievement sweep every 30 min, goals/notify ticks, routine auto-ticks, Daily Review words), so the iPad is redrawn under the user regularly. This is the root of the reported iPad resets.

title: Quiz answers are almost always A or B, and options are never shuffled
evidence: cm/metrics.json ansDist per leaf; js/engines/quiz.js:66 (Shuffle shuffles order only), :88-96 (item.opts rendered in order, answer compared to item.ans at :113); e.g. js/data/content/maths-mech-m7.js:305-306 (every item ans: 0); shots/content-maths/m73-quiz-ipad.png (Q1 answer A)
rootCause: Authors put the right answer first (bank authors second), and the engine trusts the authored order.
fix: In mountMCQ, shuffle a per-question option permutation at mount and on Retry, seeded per attempt, and map clicks back to the original index so the stats and the why text stay valid. Optionally also rebalance the authored ans positions so a fixed order is fair too.

KOS.quiz.mountMCQ renders opts in authored order, and its Shuffle button only reorders the questions. title: A curriculum fork silently hides later curriculum upgrades (plausible cause of "M7.3 is basically bare")
evidence: js/core/edits.js:1-60 (no base hash or staleness check: grep for stale/baseHash finds nothing); git log -- js/data/content/maths-mech-m7.js (a9f64b5, 4d791ca); shots/content-maths/m73-mac.png (shipped content present)

When the shipped hash differs, show a banner on the tab: "The curriculum for this topic was updated after you edited it: View new · Keep mine · Merge (append your rows)". title: Wrong flashcard answer: 9.3 Newton–Raphson from x0 = 0 gives x1 = −2.5, not 2.5
evidence: js/data/content/bank-maths-pure-c.js:646
rootCause: An arithmetic sign slip in the bank author's answer, with no automated check on numeric answers.
fix: Rewrite the card, e.g. "Where would NR fail for $f(x)=x^3-2x-5$?" → "Where $f'(x_0)=0$: $x_0=\pm\sqrt{2/3}$". Or keep the x0 = 0 example with "$x_1=-2.5$ (far from the root 2.09)". Keep its schedule key (invariant 87).

In fact f(0) = −5 and f′(0) = −2, so x1 = 0 − (−5)/(−2) = −2.5, which the card's own formula (2x³+5)/(3x²−2) also gives. The question also states something false: it says the method fails and the answer says it does not.

title: Mind ladder: most F1 concepts can never climb past Recall/Apply — 5 of 16 concepts have no route to any rung above Recall, only 3 can reach Evaluate

rootCause: Ladder rules require per-concept evidence sources that the F1 content file only provides for the lesson 'main' concepts; nothing checks reachability.
fix: Either author a route for every rung of every concept (apply items for each fallacy/premise/deduction; explain-back key points or checkpoint rubric rows for the rest), or let a concept declare which rungs it has (`rungs: ['Recall','Apply']`) and draw/count only those, computing the hero bars and 'furthest' over reachable rungs. smoke110 should assert every concept has a source for every rung it shows.
detail: The ladder (invariant 137) is derived from four evidence sources: Explain = an explain-back on a lesson whose `main` is the concept, or a checkpoint rubric row; Apply = a check/checkpoint item marked `apply` for the concept; Evaluate = a position on a contested lesson teaching the concept, or an Evaluate rubric row. Enumerating F1's authored content against those rules: premise, deduction, straw-man, false-dilemma and bandwagon have NO Explain, Apply or Evaluate source (they can only ever reach Recall); conclusion, soundness, ad-hominem, slippery-slope reach Recall+Apply only; standard-form has Explain but no Apply; steelman has no Explain (F1.7 is contested, so its prompt is a position). Only induction, charity and steelman can reach Evaluate. Yet every met concept is drawn with four rungs, the desk hero shows 'Evaluate 0%' bars computed over all met concepts and 'furthest' needs half the met concepts on a rung — so a learner who does every piece of F1 perfectly still sees Explain ≈ 38%, Evaluate ≈ 19% and four-rung ladders that cannot be completed, with no hint why.

title: Checkpoint pays 50 XP / 12 gold / +4 HP and marks itself passed with nothing right; a retake then erases the Explain/Evaluate rungs it gave

rootCause: recordCheckpoint has no pass condition and replaces the record on every attempt
fix: Define a pass rule (e.g. ≥ 2 of 3 scenarios right and ≥ half the rubric) and pay only on the first PASS, saying what is missing otherwise; keep the best attempt (merge apply/ticks by OR, or store attempts and read the best) so a retake never lowers a rung.

Cards are self-marked 'Had it/Not quite' and apply scenarios can all be wrong — 0 of 8 cards, 0 of 3 scenarios, 0 rubric points and a one-character bullet still pay the full checkpoint reward and tick F1.8's 'Check passed'. (Japanese's checkpoint requires 80% in every skill; the Mind plan's 'unit checkpoint 50/12/+4' reads as a passed checkpoint.) Separately, Retake overwrites `apply` and `synth.ticks` wholesale, so a retake with fewer rubric ticks removes Explain (argument, hidden-premise) and Evaluate (induction, steelman) that the first attempt earned.

title: Apply and Explain rungs are earned without showing understanding: Apply after the check has revealed the answer, Explain from one one-character bullet

rootCause: answerCheck records ok on any later right answer; saveExplain trusts ticks with no text threshold
fix: Count Apply only when the scenario is right at the FIRST attempt of a visit (or on a later day, with the answer not revealed in the same session); for a retried item show 'Right, but it counts next time'. For Explain require a minimum (e.g. ≥ 3 bullets or ~20 words) before ticks count, and order the prompt after the pages.
detail: Leniency of the derived ladder with thin evidence: (1) Apply = 'a scenario answered right'. A wrong answer immediately marks the right option '✓ Right' (js/modules/mindtopic.js:103-106) and offers 'Next, and come back to this'; coming back, clicking the option that was just revealed records ok:true (answerCheck keeps the first ok) and the concept reaches Apply — so every Apply rung (and the check pass that pays 12 XP) can be had by guessing once. (2) Explain = ≥60% of key points self-ticked; the text itself is not checked at all, so a single bullet 'x' with 3 of 4 ticks reaches Explain, and the explain-back can be written before a single page is read.

title: Import only reads the first line as the header: midata with a leading blank line or a semicolon delimiter, and Online Banking CSV with an account preamble, all fail

title: A met goal stays 'Met' after its target is raised or a manual count is lowered (10% shown as Met)

title: Todoist: a reminder made on one device is duplicated when another device syncs before the state document arrives
evidence: exp/td.js twodev → local 'Made on A': [[3,'T3'],[4,'T3']], remote: ['T3']; js/core/exttasks.js:180-187 (import with no matching attempt), js/core/ext.js:306-316 (syncProvider takes the lease without pulling the cloud state first), js/core/exttasks.js:229-237
rootCause: Remote link state is replicated asynchronously while the remote cursor (sync token) is per device; import has no identity check beyond byLink.
fix: Make the cycle state-consistent: before taking the lease run a cloud pull (KOS.cloudsync cycle) and push the state right after the cycle; and in reconcile's import path, before adding, look for an existing reminder already linked to that remote id (dedupe byLink after any merge) or an unlinked one in the same list whose uuidOf('add|'+uid) is pending (record pending adds {uid→temp} in state.ext so any device can recognise its own item_add). Also add a boot/merge pass that folds two reminders linked to the same ext.id.
detail: The lease serialises Todoist network work between devices, but the LINK (reminder.ext.id) lives in the synced state document, which reaches the other device later. Device A pushes a new reminder (item_add) and links it locally; device B takes the lease next (A releases it at once) while its state still holds the reminder unlinked and its own per-device sync token predates the add. B's incremental pull returns the new Todoist task, finds no local link (byLink) and reconcile() imports it as a SECOND reminder linked to the same Todoist id; the cloud merge then keeps both (different ids/uids). Reproduced in jsdom with the smoke112 fake: after the B-side cycle, two local reminders 'Made on A' are both linked to T3 while Todoist has one task. With a Mac, iPad and iPhone all open this is the ordinary case, matching the user's 'many problems between Reminders and Todoist'.

title: Todoist: a failed second command batch leaves the first batch's tasks unlinked, so the next sync imports them as duplicates
evidence: exp/td.js chunk → 'cycle1 false Todoist answered 503 / remote items 45 local linked 0 / cycle2: local total 105 dup local 45'; js/core/exttasks.js:318-335 (ok callbacks only after the reduce over chunks resolves), js/core/exttasks.js:241-243 (token saved only after push)
rootCause: Non-atomic multi-request push with all-or-nothing local bookkeeping.
fix: Apply each chunk's results as soon as it returns (run the after[] entries whose commands are all in that chunk's sync_status), keep an item's parent and sub-task adds in one chunk, and persist the link/temp-id map before the next request; on the pull side, treat an incoming task whose id appears in a stored temp_id_mapping as already linked.
detail: tdPush sends commands in chunks of 90 and runs every 'ok' callback (which writes the link and base) only after ALL chunks succeed. If chunk 2 fails (HTTP 429/5xx, offline, tab suspended), chunk 1's item_add commands have already created tasks in Todoist but nothing local is linked, and the sync token is not saved either. The next cycle pulls those tasks with the old token, finds no local link and imports each as a new reminder; the originals are then re-sent as item_add. Linking a list with ~45+ reminders that have a sub-task each exceeds 90 commands on the first cycle. Reproduced: 60 reminders with one sub each, chunk 2 answered 503 → cycle 2 leaves 105 local reminders (45 duplicates).

title: First cloud sign-in silently discards a device's reminders, assignments, exams, routines and other data that 'stateMeaningful' does not count
evidence: exp/cs.js → {before:{rem:1,asg:1}, after:{rem:[],asg:[]}, cloudHasLocal:false}; js/core/cloudsync.js:234-251 (stateMeaningful), 975-990 (assessLink), 758-773 (not dirty → replaceState)
rootCause: A hand-maintained allowlist of 'real data' that was not extended as new domains were added; replaceState used as the adopt path.
fix: Define 'meaningful' as 'differs from a freshly booted DEFAULTS document' (hash syncableState against a boot-time pristine snapshot, ignoring known seeders such as SAMPLE events and pacing seed), or enumerate every record array in cloudmerge RECORDS plus the keyed maps; and on first link always take the no-base three-way merge (union) instead of replaceState when the local side has ANY record. Snapshot the local state into the media kv before any replaceState so it can be restored.
detail: assessLink classifies each side with stateMeaningful(), which only looks at progress, sessions, custom cards, wishlist, tracker entries, goals, non-sample calendar events and Governor xp/gold/owned. A device whose data is reminders, assignments, Exams-hub assessments, routines, Pacing ticks, Money settings, curriculum edits, Code/Japanese/Mind/Creatives evidence or SRS state (without a logged session) counts as EMPTY, so linking it to an account that has data takes the 'remoteOnly' path: adoptRemote → applyRemoteState with no lastPushedHash → dirty = stateMeaningful(local) = false → KOS.store.replaceState(incoming). The local records are replaced without a merge, a toast or a backup. Reproduced in jsdom with smoke17's fake Supabase: a fresh device adds one reminder and one assignment, signs in to an account with history; after syncNow both are gone and the cloud copy never received them. A Home Screen install on the iPad has its own storage separate from Safari, so 'used it a bit before signing in' is a realistic path. The mirror case ('localOnly' when the remote only holds such records) overwrites the remote the same way.

title: Two open tabs or windows overwrite each other's saves (last writer wins on the whole state)
devices: mac (two windows/tabs), iPad Safari with two tabs
evidence: kos.mjs eval 17 (iframe experiment) → {afterBsaved:true, finalHasA:true, finalHasB:false, inMemA_hasB:false}; js/core/store.js:395-410 (whole-document save), no 'storage' listener anywhere in js/ (grep)
rootCause: localStorage used as a single-writer store without cross-tab coordination.
fix: Listen for 'storage' on the state key and, when another tab wrote, three-way merge the incoming document into memory with KOS.cloudmerge (base = last document this tab wrote/read) before the next save; or elect one writer tab with navigator.locks / BroadcastChannel and make other tabs read-only with a banner. At minimum detect a foreign write (compare a per-save nonce) and reload instead of overwriting.
detail: Each tab keeps its own in-memory KOS.store.state and save() writes the WHOLE document to localStorage 120 ms later; nothing listens for the 'storage' event, and there is no BroadcastChannel or Web Lock. A change made in one tab is erased by the next save in the other. Reproduced on the slot with an iframe of index.html (same origin, same localStorage): tab B added 'TAB-B reminder' and saved; tab A then added its own reminder; the stored document holds A's and not B's, and tab A never learns of B's. Both tabs also mint the same nextId. With cloud sync the shared IndexedDB meta (seq, lastPushedHash, base) can let the stale tab's CAS succeed and upload a document without the other tab's record. On the MacBook a second window or a PWA window beside a tab is ordinary.

title: Todoist: a full sync drops completed sub-tasks from the reminder (and can re-add them to Todoist as duplicates)
evidence: exp/td.js subs → 'after remote sub tick: [[Plan,true],[Draft,false]]' then 'after full sync: [[Draft,false]]'; js/core/exttasks.js:217-220 (token '*' on any link change, mirror reset), 108-113 (childrenOf reads only the mirror), 296-307 (missing x → item_add)
rootCause: Absence in a full sync is interpreted as deletion.
fix: Do not reset the mirror on a full sync triggered by a link change; only drop entries of projects no longer linked. Treat a sub missing from a full sync as 'unknown', not deleted (keep subs whose remote child is not returned unless is_deleted arrives), and never re-add a sub that has an x.
detail: When the linked-project signature changes (linking or unlinking any list) the cycle requests sync_token '*' and resets the mirror. Todoist's full sync returns only active items, so completed sub-tasks are absent from the mirror; the parent's remote subs then differ from base and the pull overwrites the local subs, deleting every ticked sub-task. If the local subs were also edited, local wins, and each local sub whose x is no longer in the mirror is sent again as item_add, duplicating it in Todoist. Reproduced with a fake that, like Todoist, omits checked items from a full sync: 'Plan' (ticked) vanished locally after linking a second list. Depends on Todoist excluding completed sub-items from a full sync (documented behaviour for completed tasks).

title: Todoist: completing a repeating reminder here sends a new due string instead of closing the occurrence
evidence: exp/td.js recur → cmds [[{type:item_update,args:{id:T1,due:{date:'2026-11-05',string:'every week',is_recurring:true}}}]]; gym: local done=true, cmds [[item_close]]; js/core/reminders.js:229-236, js/core/exttasks.js:99-107, 282-290
rootCause: Local recurrence semantics duplicated instead of delegated to the provider that owns the rule.
fix: For a linked repeating reminder, push item_close (Todoist rolls the date itself) and let the pull bring the new date back; treat ext.rs rules as repeating in complete() (roll forward with Todoist as the source) so both paths behave alike.
detail: KOS.reminders.complete() rolls a repeating reminder forward locally (new due, done=false) so the push sees only a 'when' change and sends item_update with due {date: next, string: 'every week', is_recurring}. Todoist never records the completion (no history/karma, completed view empty), and since Todoist parses due.string, the explicit date may be ignored and re-anchored to today, which the next pull brings back. For a Todoist-only rule (ext.rs, e.g. 'every mon, fri') the reminder instead closes locally (recur is null here) and sends item_close, so it shows as completed until the next pull un-completes it with Todoist's new date: two different behaviours for the same action.

title: An assignment re-keyed by the cloud merge leaves its goals, Exams links, Focus sessions and review picks pointing at another assignment
evidence: js/core/cloudmerge.js:57-58 (assignments refs: calendar.events only), 293-346 (rekeyCollisions rewrites only spec.refs); references listed above
rootCause: Counter ids plus a hand-maintained reference list that new features did not extend.
fix: Add every reference to RECORDS[].refs (goals.items links.assignmentId as a nested field, exams.assessments links.assignmentId, sessions metrics.assignmentId and metrics.segments[].assignmentId, dayReview picks), or move assignments/reminders/events to random string ids as Money, Routines and Exams already do (the long-term fix).
detail: Ids are per-device counters; when two devices mint the same assignment id between syncs, rekeyCollisions re-keys the local one and rewrites only RECORDS[].refs. For assignments.items that list is calendar.events.assignmentId alone, but assignment ids are also stored in goals (links.assignmentId, js/core/goals.js:130), Exams assessments (links.assignmentId, js/core/exams.js:178, 536, 726), session entries and their segments (metrics.assignmentId, js/core/sessions.js:93-98; Focus banks minutes by it), and Daily Review picks (js/core/dayreview.js:489). After a re-key those references silently follow the OTHER device's assignment: minutes, goal progress and an exam's linked coursework attach to the wrong record. Reminders have the same gap (reminder ids referenced by the review picks).

title: A 404 on an update deletes the local event or reminder (e.g. after reconnecting a different Google account)
evidence: js/core/extgcal.js:419-421, js/core/exttasks.js:416-417, js/core/ext.js:241-250
rootCause: A failed write is treated as proof of a remote deletion.
fix: On 404 for an update, unlink the record (ext = null, keep it local, count it as 'unlinked' in the status) instead of deleting it; delete locally only from a pull that reports the item cancelled/deleted. Clear (or archive) ext links on disconnect and on connecting a different account (compare the account id).
detail: When a PATCH to Google Calendar or Google Tasks answers 404/410, the cycle deletes the LOCAL record inside inbound(): extgcal.js:421 KOS.calendar.deleteEvent(ev.id), exttasks.js:417 KOS.reminders.remove(it.id). disconnect() (ext.js:241-250) clears only the kv (sync tokens, mirrors) and leaves every record's ext link in place, so connecting a different Google account (or the event being moved to another calendar) turns the next local edit of any linked event or reminder into a silent local deletion, with no undo and no notice. This contradicts the 'never inferred from absence' intent of invariant 158 and is the opposite of Todoist's behaviour (an update to a missing item there is just retried forever, exttasks.js:330-333).

title: The full backup leaves out saved Reports and snapshots, and builds one giant string that can fail on the iPad
evidence: js/core/store.js:513-583 (no reportStore step; JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) at 588), js/core/reportstore.js (no exportAll), js/modules/attachments.js:454-480 (base64 for every blob)
rootCause: Backup coverage list maintained by hand; whole-document serialisation.
fix: Add KOS.reportStore.exportAll/importAll to the snapshot; stream the backup (build the Blob from parts: a JSON head plus one part per file, no indentation) or offer 'backup without files' when files exceed ~100 MB; report per-section failures like importFull does instead of failing the whole export.
detail: store.snapshotFull collects state, media, attachments (kurenai-os-files, every binary as base64), money, reviews, mind, ink and creatives, but not kurenai-os-reports (saved weeks/months/terms/years, their Kurenai words and the boundary snapshots that status moves need — 'never recomputed', invariant 101/102). Signed out, a restore on a new device loses every saved report and snapshot for good. The backup is serialised with JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) into a single Blob: with a few hundred MB of files (the app asks for persistent storage at 200 MB) the base64 plus indentation is a string of several hundred MB, which risks an out-of-memory reload on iPad Safari, and that failure is silent (no error reaches done()). A failing sub-export (e.g. creatives) aborts the whole backup instead of reporting the missing part.

title: The whole state lives in one localStorage key with no fallback: when it outgrows the quota every later change is lost on reload
evidence: kos.mjs eval 17 → state 372,924 chars; srs 110,391; sessions 84,052; pacing 84,696; 5,436 curriculum cards; quota experiment → errs ['Kurenai OS: save failed QuotaExceededError…'], stored:false, toast 'Save failed — storage may be full. Export your data.'; js/core/store.js:395-425
rootCause: Single-key localStorage persistence for an unbounded document.
fix: Move the large, append-heavy parts (srs/cards, the session ledger, Japanese facets, Mind cards) into IndexedDB records like the review log, or store the document in IndexedDB with localStorage as a small boot cache; show the state size in Archive › Storage with a warning at 60% of quota; on a failed save keep a persistent banner (not a toast) and retry into IndexedDB.
detail: Measured on the seeded account: the state document is 372,924 characters in one key (kurenai-os-v1); srs is 110 KB for 675 rated cards (164 B a card), sessions 84 KB for 600 (140 B each, capped at 2,000), pacing 85 KB. The curriculum alone has 5,436 flashcards, so a fully reviewed deck is ~0.9 MB before Code, Japanese facets and Mind cards, and every new domain adds to the same document. Chrome refused the write at ~5.2 M characters total; WebKit's limit is of the same order. When setItem throws, save() shows one toast ('Save failed — storage may be full. Export your data.') and keeps running on the in-memory copy; every later change, and the pagehide flush (which only logs, store.js:417-425), is lost on the next reload or when iOS evicts the page. Reproduced by filling localStorage on the slot: the save failed with QuotaExceededError and the change was not stored. There is no size readout in Archive › Storage for the state document, and no migration of the big parts (srs, sessions, facets) to IndexedDB.

title: Every replicated store pulls with a strict updated_at > cursor on now() stamps, so a row committed late is skipped forever
evidence: supabase/migrations/20260716000001_kos_sync_init.sql:26-35 (now()); q.gt('updated_at', …) at js/core/money.js:1126, reviewlog.js:133, mindjournal.js:191, inksync.js:97, reportstore.js:324, cloudsync.js:358/376; cursor = max seen (money.js:1189, 1207)
rootCause: Timestamp cursor over transaction-start timestamps.
fix: Stamp with clock_timestamp() in the trigger and pull with an overlap window (gt cursor − 2 minutes) — every store already skips its own echo by stamp or uid, so re-reading a few rows is harmless; or use a monotonic bigserial 'version' column per table as the cursor.
detail: Media, files, money, reviews, mind, ink, reports and push all pull 'updated_at > cursor' and then advance the cursor to the largest updated_at seen. The touch trigger stamps updated_at := now(), which in Postgres is the TRANSACTION START time. If device A's upsert (a 500-row media chunk, a money batch) starts at t1 and commits after device B's quicker write stamped t2 > t1, a third device that pulls between the two commits sets its cursor to t2 and never fetches A's rows (t1 < t2). Nothing ever re-reads them: the pulling device silently lacks those transactions/reviews/ink strokes until a restore. With three devices syncing on focus this is a real, if rare, divergence with no symptom.

title: Todoist: a command the server rejects is resent on every cycle forever, with no status shown
evidence: js/core/exttasks.js:329-334 (only the all-ok case is handled; errors in r.sync_status are dropped), js/core/exttasks.js:256 (delete queue entry kept on error)
rootCause: Error results of batched commands are ignored.
fix: Read sync_status errors: for 'not found' (error_code 22) drop the queue entry or unlink the record; for other errors record them in counts and setStatus so Connections shows 'n changes refused' with the reason; apply per-command bookkeeping rather than per group.
detail: tdPush applies a record's bookkeeping only when every command in its group returns 'ok'. A rejected command (item_update or item_delete for a task deleted or moved out of reach in Todoist, an invalid label, a due string Todoist cannot parse) leaves base and the delete queue unchanged, so the same command is sent every cycle (every few minutes and on every focus) and the Connections status still says the cycle succeeded, because sync_status errors are never turned into counts or an error. title: An unreadable stored state is replaced by a fresh one and overwritten on the next save

rootCause: The redraw stopgap's hold list is a hand-maintained set of view ids in ui.js; any page added later with transient in-page state is unprotected by default.
fix: Short term: add governor (the edit arg) and any page with an in-page draft to the held list, or let a view declare itself held (e.g. KOS.views.x.holdsDraft = arg => …) so the list is not a central guess. Proper fix: the view lifecycle in the backlog (a view can veto or persist its draft before a redraw); the Edit seat draft could also live in state.ui like other per-device drafts.
detail: #/governor/edit keeps its draft (showcase, background, title, sigil) in a closure inside the view function (js/modules/governor-ui.js:660-686). The kos-redraw-1 stopgap holds background redraws only for TASK_VIEWS (js/core/ui.js:357-358), which does not list governor (nor achievements, money, goals, routines). So a soft background redraw (routines autoSync after a session or on the review ticker, js/core/routines.js:699; the Daily Review closing, js/modules/dayreview.js:92/103/661/709; the Google read-only copy loading, js/core/ext.js:364; own art loading at boot, js/main.js:307) remounts the page at once, and a cloud pull (hard) does so 45 s after the last touch. Repro on slot 20: open Edit your seat, Background tab, pick another background (Save lights up, data-state=lit), call KOS.rerender({background:'soft'}): the tab is back on Showcase, the picked background is gone and Save is no longer lit; nothing was saved. The page has a Discard/Save pair, so the user believes the draft is held until they press one. Top-up 2: the Wall's Showcase tab has the same problem: its picker draft (with its own Save button, js/modules/achievements.js:412-413) is lost on a soft background redraw because achievements is not in TASK_VIEWS either: picked 1 badge (count 1 of 6) -> KOS.rerender({background:soft}) -> 0 of 6, nothing stored.

title: Badge measuring runs synchronously on the main thread: the Governor's Seat measures all 254 badges twice per render, and every topic tick re-measures 44 study badges
evidence: arch20/prof-governor.txt (CPU profile of KOS.show('governor')); eval on slot 20: {listCallsPerGovernorRender:2, list first 3929 ms / second 138 ms, evalStudy 13555 then 3112 then 1324 ms}, longtask observer after KOS.achievements.onProgress('cs') = [541]; js/core/achievements.js:239-262, 296-341, 446-466; js/modules/governor-ui.js:358, 527, 732; arch20/bootsteps.mjs [show 13708 ms on the Wall]; arch20/views-out.txt; eval longtasks after touch [920,631]; savesPerNoopSweep 0
rootCause: list() and evaluate() both measure from scratch with a per-call context; measures reuse un-memoised derived reads; all of it runs synchronously.
fix: Keep the last evaluate's per-badge values (in memory, keyed by a store revision or the ledgerKey already computed at achievements.js:134) and let list() read them instead of re-measuring; measure only when the owning domain's revision moved. Run the domain re-measure in idle slices (requestIdleCallback, a few badges per slice) so a tick never blocks input. The memo layer for readiness/code evidence recommended in the backlog would cut the rest.
detail: KOS.achievements.list() builds a fresh context (makeCtx, js/core/achievements.js:239) and runs every badge's measure (measureOne, :296) each time it is called; nothing is memoised across calls or renders. The Governor's Seat status page calls it twice per render (js/modules/governor-ui.js:358 the arc of medals and :527 the area cards) and Edit your seat once more (:732); the Wall calls it on each tab (js/modules/achievements.js:126, 613, 747). Many measures are themselves the expensive derived reads the earlier audit found un-memoised — KOS.exams.readiness for every upcoming exam (achcatalogue.js:251-256, the 'Ready' badge), Code/Creatives/Mind evidence over every lesson, topic bands over every leaf for the ~30 unit badges (reg.unit, achcatalogue.js ~246). Owner events re-measure by domain (touch, 400 ms debounce), and the 'study' domain holds 44 badges, so every store.setCheck/setStatus (js/core/store.js:452/466 → onProgress) costs one main-thread long task some 400 ms after the tick. Measured on the dense account (machine shared, load 5-9, so absolute figures are inflated): a single onProgress('cs') produced one 541 ms long task; evaluate(['study']) took 1.3-13.5 s across runs; KOS.achievements.list() 2.4-3.9 s cold, 138 ms warm; KOS.show('governor') 0.7-22 s (3.1 s typical first render), with measureOne, reg.unit, readiness, code/creatives/mind evidence, code.stats and srs.dueCards at the top of its CPU profile. Top-up 2 (load 7-10): KOS.achievements.touch([study]) produced long tasks of 920 and 631 ms; a reload that restores onto #/achievements made its first KOS.show take 13.7 s in the boot wrapper; the Wall shows Reading your records for 1.9-7.9 s on first open and re-measures on every tab switch and every rerender (4.4 s). A no-op full sweep writes nothing (0 store.save calls), which is correct. Measure exceptions are swallowed to null with no console line (achievements.js:307), so a schema change in an owner would silently stop a badge.

title: Opening a Wall set by link and leaving before the badges are measured pops the set dialog over whatever page you are on
evidence: shots/architecture-perf/ach-set-dialog-over-home.png; eval on slot 20: {view:home, hash:#/home, dialog:CS, Maths and IT Study ... Into the green, after:911}; js/modules/achievements.js:126-135
rootCause: A wrong staleness check (parentNode of an inner node is never null) on an async render callback; no shared per-view cancellation token.
fix: Make the guard `if (!body.isConnected) return;` (or compare a render token / KOS.currentNav() with the one at call time), and the same in governor-ui.js:358/527/732, whose callbacks have no guard at all. Long term: the view lifecycle (AbortController per view) recommended in the backlog.
detail: KOS.views.achievements draws the Wall in the async KOS.achievements.list() callback (js/modules/achievements.js:126-135) and opens the set dialog there for #/achievements/set/<id>. The guard meant to stop a stale callback, `if (!body.isConnected && body.parentNode == null) return;` (:127), can never fire: body is a child of root, so body.parentNode is root even after KOS.show has emptied #main. So the callback draws into a detached tree and then calls openSetDialog on the new page. list() measures all 254 badges and takes 0.3-8 s on the dense account, so it is easy to leave in time (a set link from the bell, search or the Governor, then Back). Repro on slot 20 (seeded): KOS.show(achievements, set/study); 50 ms later KOS.show(home) -> 0.9 s later the Into the green set dialog is open over Home (URL #/home); after the earlier render-timing pass three such dialogs were stacked (role=dialog count 3).

title: Every boot runs the exam cap pass over all cards (0.7-1 s) and readiness about fifteen times before the first page settles
evidence: node arch20/bootsteps.mjs 20 → [show 13708 ms (the restored Wall), today.build 2830, srs.examPass 2772, exams.readiness 1826, 658, 97, 86 ... x15, exams.freezePass 203]; eval: examPass 1010 ms then 712 ms, returns 0; readiness over 11 upcoming exams 1300 ms; js/main.js:138; js/core/srs.js:182-222
rootCause: Pure derive-on-read functions with linear lookups, called from several boot paths without a memo or a changed-inputs check.
fix: Build a Set of leaf keys per exam once in examIndex (or a leaf->exam map) so examFor is O(1); hoist weights(); run examPass only when its inputs changed (a hash of the cap list and the exam-day target kept in state.srsCfg) or in an idle callback after first paint. Memoise readiness per assessment on a store revision (the memo layer in the backlog).
detail: main.js:138 calls KOS.srs.examPass() synchronously on every boot. It walks every scheduled card and, for each, examFor() searches every capped exam with e.leaves.indexOf(sid:ref) — a linear scan of an array of leaf keys (js/core/srs.js:182-191, 201-222), so the cost is cards x exams x leaves, and recordMemory/weights() is recomputed per card. On the dense account (5,442 cards, 11 upcoming assessments) one pass takes 0.7-1.0 s and moves nothing (returns 0) — it is only useful the first boot after an exam is added. In the same boot KOS.exams.readiness ran 15 times (1.8 s, 0.7 s and a dozen of 50-100 ms; Home focus plan, notices, the badge sweep and predictedAtExam each re-derive it), and today.build 2.8 s. Measured with a boot wrapper (arch20/bootsteps.mjs; machine at load 6-7, so absolute figures are inflated about 2-3x, the ratios hold).

title: The smoke gate is not reliable under load: five suites fail when run three at a time and pass alone
evidence: arch20/gate-summary.txt (exit code, ms, suite; sorted by time); scratchpad logs: smoke4 'STEP anime vault renders + lazy fallback…: Error: no cards rendered' tools/smoke4.test.js:390; smoke17 'applyCosmetics was not called after a remote state applied'; smoke16 TypeError tools/smoke16.test.js:550; serial re-runs all exit 0
rootCause: Tests wait fixed times for async work (IndexedDB, timers) inside jsdom.
fix: Replace fixed sleeps in those five suites with waits on a condition (poll for the cards, the announcement, the applyCosmetics call); then add a parallel runner (npm test) with a per-suite timeout.
detail: Running all 113 suites with three in parallel on the shared test machine (load ~10) failed smoke2, smoke4 (vault cards not rendered in jsdom), smoke16 (wishlist cover), smoke17 (applyCosmetics not called after a pull) and smoke45 (toast announcements). Each passed when re-run alone (2-16 s). The failures are timing assumptions (fixed waits in the tests) rather than product bugs, but they make a parallel runner — the obvious answer to the gate's 20-minute CPU cost — unusable, and they would read as regressions on a slow CI machine. The gate itself is now 1,227 CPU-seconds (450 s wall with three workers); smoke56 (242 s) and smoke75 (236 s) are 39% of it.

title: iPhone: most text fields and selects are under 16px, so iOS Safari zooms the page on every focus
evidence: css/base.css:156-160 (rule inside @layer base); css/tokens.css:35 (@layer tokens, base, layout, components, views, themes); overriding rules e.g. css/components.css:406 .k-input, :417 .k-pill-select font-size var(--fs-12-5), css/views/assistant.css:216 .k-asst-input font-size var(--fs-14-5); measurement audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/a11y-iphone.jsonl (font16 lists per view, script a11y-scan.js) | Re-check 6 Nov 2026 (kos-redraw-1): Re-measured at 402x874 on kos-redraw-1 (a11y21-iphone.jsonl): Assistant composer 14.5px, Focus topic/objective inputs 13.5px, Files search 13.5px, Shrine/Wishlist status selects 12.5px, Seasonal year select 12.5px; the new picture drawer's condition selects are .k-input--sm too (js/modules/artslot.js:69). css/base.css:156-160 still sits in @layer base.
rootCause: Cascade-layer order: a base-layer guard cannot override component-layer declarations.
fix: Move the phone 16px rule to the last layer (themes, or an unlayered rule at the end of components.css) so it wins: @media (max-width:700px){ input:not([type=checkbox]):not([type=radio]):not([type=range]), select, textarea, [contenteditable] { font-size: max(16px, 1em) !important } } — or set --fs-input tokens that components read. Add a smoke check that no visible field computes under 16px at 402px.
detail: Invariant 40 promises 16px inputs on the phone, and base.css sets input, select, textarea { font-size: max(16px, 1em) } under max-width 700px. That rule lives in @layer base, which the declared order (tokens, base, layout, components, views, themes) puts BELOW every component and view rule, so any class that sets a font size wins. Measured at 402x874: Assistant composer 14.5px, Reminders quick-add 14px, Focus topic/objective inputs 13.5px, Help search 13px, Files search 13.5px, Backup & Restore e-mail/password 13.5px, Routines settings times 13.5px, Media Sync inputs 13.5px, Assignments subtask input 13px, every .k-pill-select sort/filter (Assignments, Exams & Papers, Shrine, Wishlist, topic page reader select, Card stats retention) 12.5px, Pacing lesson-day selects 12px, vault score corners 14px. On the user's iPhone each of these zooms the viewport when tapped and leaves it zoomed (the layout then scrolls sideways until pinched back). Only the phone search sheet was special-cased (layout.css:457).

title: Undo in toasts cannot be reached by keyboard or screen reader
evidence: js/core/ui.js:72-87 (tabindex '-1' at :76, 8000 ms timer :81, announce(msg) without the action); index.html:140 (#toast aria-hidden=true); callers js/modules/dayreview.js:534,615,621,622, js/modules/reminders.js:344 | Re-check 6 Nov 2026 (kos-redraw-1): Re-read js/core/ui.js:72-87 (tabindex -1, 8000 ms, announce(msg) only) and index.html:141 (#toast aria-hidden=true).
rootCause: #toast was made purely visual in Phase F; the later action variant reused it without restoring access.
fix: Give action toasts a focusable, named Undo: drop tabindex=-1 and aria-hidden on the action toast (or render action toasts in a non-hidden region), announce 'msg. Undo available (Ctrl/Cmd+Z)', pause the timer on hover/focus, and add a global Cmd/Ctrl+Z that runs the latest toast action.

The toast disappears after 8 s with no pause on hover/focus (WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard, 2.2.1 Timing). A keyboard or VoiceOver user has no undo for these actions.

title: Focus chime is silent on iPhone/iPad and has no on/off or volume setting
evidence: js/modules/focus.js:788-801 (chime(): new AC() on first call from tick, no ctx.resume()); call sites :496, :508, :522 inside the interval tick; grep -rniE '"(Sound|Chime)' js/modules js/core → none | Re-check 6 Nov 2026 (kos-redraw-1): js/modules/focus.js:788-800 unchanged: AudioContext created lazily at chime time with no unlock on a gesture and no setting.
rootCause: Audio unlock rules of iOS WebKit not handled; no audio preference model.
fix: Create/resume the AudioContext in Start's click handler (unlock it), call ctx.resume() before each chime, and add a Focus setting 'Sound at cycle end' (on/off + volume, per device in state.ui). Also send a device notification for cycle end when the page is hidden.
detail: The only sound in the app (Pomodoro cycle end, break end, stopwatch break nudge) is a Web Audio oscillator whose AudioContext is created lazily inside the timer tick, never from a user gesture and never resume()d. WebKit starts such a context 'suspended', so on the user's iPhone and iPad the chime never plays; the cue is then only a 2.6 s toast that a user away from the screen will miss. There is also no setting anywhere to turn the chime off, choose a sound or set its volume (grep finds no Sound/Chime control). Japanese voice lines and the Assistant's speech are the only other audio.

title: Touch-size floor is undone by shared primitives: pill selects 30px, switches 34x20, checkboxes 18x18 on iPad and iPhone
evidence: css/base.css:115-121 (:where(...) floor; no input[type=checkbox], no .k-switch); css/components.css:417 (.k-pill-select { min-block-size: 0 } cancels it); css/components.css:207 (.k-switch fixed --fx-switch-w/h, not in the coarse block at :669-677); css/layout.css:233-235 (.k-rail-toggle at --hit-dense); measurements audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/a11y-ipad.jsonl, a11y-iphone.jsonl | Re-check 6 Nov 2026 (kos-redraw-1): Under touch at 820x1180 and 402x874: switches still 34x20 on the new Avatar & profile page (gov.theme-follow, gov.art-on, gov.art-reduced), the Wall's List view, Focus penalty, Pen and ink, Exams; Seasonal year select 96x31; the Assistant's Pin/Hide/Voice chips 21px tall (see the Assistant finding).
rootCause: The floor is a zero-specificity base rule; primitives set their own sizes after it.
fix: In the components coarse block add: .k-pill-select { min-block-size: var(--hit-coarse) }; .k-switch { scale or an inset ::before hit area to 44x44 } (keep the visual 34x20 but pad the label/row); input[type=checkbox]:not(.k-switch) { inline-size/block-size 24px plus a 44px label hit area }; remove min-block-size:0 from .k-pill-select. title: Tab strips declare role=tablist/tab but ignore arrow keys and have no tabpanel
